_provenance.metrics_object_removed: The reference's trailing "metrics" object is stripped from every body here: we emit no such key on any tag route. That difference is ledgered as traceql-tag-routes-metrics-object-absent and is not what this fixture is for.
_provenance.ordering: The reference does not sort tag values (ledger traceql-tag-discovery-ordering). Its span.port order here is string-then-int; ours is int-then-string. The test compares the entry SET for keys with more than one value and the exact array for single-value keys.

captures.how: One OTLP/HTTP JSON push of the issue #476 acceptance corpus (two resource groups, timestamps derived from the clock at push time), then GET /api/v2/search/tag/{key}/values per key and GET /api/search/tag/port/values.

corpus.trace_1: 1111111111111111aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa / span aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa1 "checkout"; resource service.name = STRING "12345"; scope io.otel.http 1.2.3; span attrs build="007", timeout="2s", enabled="true", ratio="1.5", slo="1.5", note="" (all STRINGS), http.status_code=int 500, sampled=bool true, cpu=double 1.5, port=STRING "8080"
corpus.trace_2: 2222222222222222bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb / span bbbbbbbbbbbbbbb2 "charge"; resource service.name = string "checkout"; span attr port=INT 8080

captures.how: One OTLP/HTTP JSON push of the C10 corpus below, then the q matrix and the range shapes over GET /api/v2/search/tag/{tag}/values, /api/search/tag/{tag}/values, /api/v2/search/tags and /api/search/tags; then a second push of the C4 typing corpus and one more name-values read over the union. Every timestamp is derived from the clock at push time.

corpus.C10: ten single-span traces: names GET /api/v1/users, GET /api/v1/users/{id}, HTTP POST, checkout-svc.process, checkout-svc.retry, 派遣クエリ, the empty string, a, pay.charge, pay.charge.retry; services cart/checkout/pay; resource deployment.environment=prod throughout; span attrs http.method (string) and http.status_code (int); status code 2 where http.status_code >= 500, else 1; kind server; duration 1.5 ms
corpus.C4: six more single-span traces under service typed, named 500, 1.5, true, 1.5s, -3 and checkout — the shapes a text-classifying type inference would call int/float/bool/duration/int/string — plus one name of 9000 ASCII characters, over the 8192-byte string-column cap

captures.why_two_endpoints: The two corpora cannot share one reference instance: measured on this build, its tag-value time filtering is BLOCK-granular, not span-granular — two corpora pushed 120 s apart were both returned by a window covering only the later one. So the #476 sections replay against their own endpoint.
captures.measured_incompleteness: Case Q-AM: with the same corpus and window, the reference answers {resource.service.name="pay"} on span.http.status_code with [201] alone, while its own name-values answer for the same condition lists the span `a`, whose http.status_code is 200 ({name="a"} returns [200]). The same shape appears for service checkout (500 only, 200 missing) and not for cart. The mechanism was not established; what is recorded is the observation.

captures.how: One OTLP/HTTP JSON push of the CQ corpus below into a freshly started, unmodified, digest-pinned reference container on ports unique to that run, then the 28 requests of the question_mark_keys section, then the container was removed. Every timestamp is derived from the clock at push time.

corpus.CQ: two single-span traces under service q509, resource attribute res.q?key="rv?1"; span q509-a (trace 50900000000000000000000000000001 / span 5090000000000001) carries k?q="vq1", a?="v-trailing", ?a="v-leading", a??b="v-double", a?b?c="v-multi", a???b="v-triple", http.target?raw="/x?y=1", plain509="v?1", a?fields="vf1", ?fields="vf2"; span q509-b (trace ...0002 / span 5090000000000002) carries k?q="vq2" and plain509="v?2". All values are strings.

captures.case_shape: Each case carries `window` (whether the request appends the corpus window) and `q`. v2 cases carry `values` as [type, value] pairs; the v1 flat route returns bare strings and its cases carry bare strings on BOTH sides. The four native-route cases carry "reference": null — that route answers 404 there.
captures.ordering: The reference does not sort its value lists and its order is not stable between identical requests: QM-A came back vq1,vq2 and QM-A2 vq2,vq1 in the same capture. Each case's reference half is stored EXACTLY as captured and compared as a multiset; ours is sorted ascending and asserted as an order.
captures.error_case: QM-T's two 400 bodies differ in wording, so the body is carried outside the compared `reference`/`pulsus` objects (as `pulsus_body`). The compared halves hold the status and the content type, on which the two sides agree — which is why this section needs no ledger row.
captures.metrics_object_removed: As for every other section here: the reference's trailing "metrics" object is stripped. Its values are not a fixed quantity either — they were observed changing between consecutive identical requests — so neither it nor the scopes-array order of /api/v2/search/tags may be read as a divergence in ours.
